html:
The Ditidaht are a First Nation of south-western Vancouver Island, around Nitinat Lake and the outer coast. Their language belongs to the southern branch of the Wakashan family and is closest to that of the Makah across the Strait of Juan de Fuca.

Like their Nuu-chah-nulth neighbours, they lived from the sea: salmon, halibut, shellfish and, in the past, whales hunted from cedar canoes. Wealth and rank were shown and passed on at the potlatch. European traders arrived on the coast in the late 1700s. Today the Ditidaht Nation is based at Nitinat Lake in British Columbia, Canada.
